answer: Unique Work Ledger. Each identity must submit a distinct, verifiable task fragment (e.g., a signed computation over a random seed) whose output is logged in a public append-only ledger; no two identities may share a fragment, and fragments are checked against a secret reachable only at the network's zenith of issuance. Duplicates collide on replay and expose the copier. An attacker pays the full compute cost of every fragment plus forfeiture of all collateral locked per fragment on collision — a fable of cheap duplication dies on that ledge.
